newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Socialists would bring in new faces, women.
newsitem.headline: French Socialists would bring in new faces, women.

text.p: There will be lots of fresh faces and "many women" in the cabinet if the left wins France's May 25-June 1 snap parliamentary election, Socialist former prime minister Laurent Fabius said on Tuesday.
"Our first decision will be to make up a cabinet, which must have many women and new faces and people who do not hold other offices at the local level," Fabius said in a radio interview.
Opinion polls show the left within striking distance of the ruling centre-right less than three weeks from the first round of the election called by conservative President Jacques Chirac.
France's practice of allowing members of parliament to simultaneously serve as mayors or hold other local offices has come under fire in the run-up to the election.
The centre-right was also criticised for sacking -- just six months after taking office in May 1995 -- eight of the 12 women in Prime Minister Alain Juppe's initial cabinet.
Fabius told France Info radio that naming the cabinet would be the left's first move should it win the election.

Its second step would be to refashion the budget "in a way which favours jobs and housing and undertakes fiscal reform, because there are clearly tax inequalities in our country which must be fixed", Fabius said.
The new government would next begin new negotiations on Europe with an aim of assuring that monetary union serves the best interests of the French people, he said.
Its fourth move would be to organise a national conference on employment, pay and a reduction in the working week, he said.
The Socialists have pledged to create 700,000 new jobs to combat France's record 12.8 percent unemployment and want to cut the working week to 35 hours from 39 hours without loss of pay.
